thread:
mina: Noticed a weird effect in the new albatross int6 bring-up: clusters look fine in float32 but after int6 the whole short-query cluster cloud appears rotated and cosine-based recall@5 drops ~3.2%.

oscar: rotated how? like a linear transform or something nonlinear?

mina: visually its like a near-orthogonal rotation + slight anisotropic scaling. Silhouette drops too (0.42 -> 0.36). This is on the short-query slice (<24 tokens), multilingual set.

taylor: do you have PCA / Procrustes alignment diffs? Procrustes residuals can indicate rotation vs shear.

mina: ran a Procrustes align float->int6 on the 10k holdout anchors. residual_norm = 0.11 (higher than typical 0.03). cos sim mean shift = -0.028.

anya: could be our quant centroid bias: low-bit quant pushes means slightly. Did you run post-quant L2 renormalize?

mina: yes we already L2-normalize after embedding. I also tried per-dim bias-correction (subtract mean on calibration) but effect persisted.

ci-bot: job 4550001234-quant-eval finished  artifacts: https://redwood-internal.s3/albatross/int6-rotation/ (private)

oscar: hypothesis list: 
- asymmetric rounding bias per-dimension
- different calibration distribution (longer contexts) -> scale mismatch
- tiny numerical instability in attention softmax kernel for short sequences

taylor: another test: compute the covariance eigenvalue spectra before/after quant. If eigenvectors are preserved but eigenvalues change, it's scaling; if eigenvectors rotate, that's alignment issue.

mina: quick spectra: float top-5 eigvals = [12.2, 7.8, 2.9, 1.1, 0.6]; int6 top-5 = [11.9, 8.0, 1.7, 0.9, 0.5]. Noticeable drop on the 3rd component.

anya: interesting. Maybe one heads projection collapsed; check per-head output variance.

oscar: also try a calibration run that constrains activation clipping per-head using short-query samples. default calibration currently mixes full-length contexts.

mina: yeah Ill run a head-aware calibrate and dump per-head var table. command I used originally:

```
python eval_onboard.py --model albatross --quant int6 --slice short_multilang --k 5 --seed 7 --out out/albatross/int6-short.json
```

mina: and calibration command Ill run next:

```
python calibrate_quant.py --model albatross --bits 6 --per_head True --dataset short_multilang_sample --out calibrations/alb-int6-headaware.json
```

taylor: also try reconstructing int6 embeddings then apply an orthogonal Procrustes-based rotation to match float. If that reduces recall gap, then rotation is main problem and we could try a small linear correction at serving time.

anya: good idea. We should measure how stable that corrective rotation is across seeds and batches. If it's stable we can ship a tiny post-process matrix.

oscar: caveat: adding a learned rotation is technically a "model change" for audit. Need to add tests to ensure no hallucination regressions for tasks using dense retrieval.

mina: practical plan: 
1) run head-aware calibration + rerun eval (mina)
2) compute Procrustes residuals and attempt offline correction matrix; measure recall lift (oscar)
3) run int7 emulation (store 6-bit pack but calibrate as 7-bit) to see gradient (taylor)
4) if rotation consistent, simulate small orthogonal post-correction and gauge stability across multilingual slices (anya)

mina: assigning 1 to myself, oscar take 2, taylor 3, anya 4?

oscar: on it. will also produce per-head var heatmap.

taylor: scripting int7 emulation now, will drop results into the artifacts bucket.

anya: if corrective rotation helps >2% recall we should consider an interim fallback to int8 for short-query routes while we finish fix.

mina: noted. quick note: latency on int6 remains attractive (~6% lower p99 CPU/gpu frames) so worth salvaging.

oscar: one more ask: please include the nearest-neighbor id-flip matrix and the proportion of flips that are within same semantic label vs different. helps understand whether rotation creates semantically bad swaps.

mina: will include that in the next artifact upload. ETA ~4h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

taylor: thanks team. ping when uploads done, will add to the onboarding dashboard. :rocket:
